glosses: lower part of a trouser leg

o.text: From Proto-Turkic *balak (“ankle; trouser leg”). Likely related to baldır.
Borrowed from Russian бе́ркут (bérkut), itself a Turkic borrowing; ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bürküt.
From Proto-Turkic *kamïĺ. Cognate with Chuvash хӑмӑл (hămăl, “stubble; stalk of cereals”).
Borrowed from Arabic عَلَيْهِ (ʕalayhi), third-person singular masculine of عَلَى (ʕalā).
